svg.title: Fullmag object, interaction, ProblemIR, and four-lane execution architecture
svg.desc: End-to-end Fullmag pipeline from fm.study authoring and scene objects (object_id, name, geometry, ObjectRegion, Material, MaterialParameterField, m0), through explicit physics modules and ordered study.stages, into ProblemIR (requested intent), the fail-closed Rust planner (fullmag-plan), four separate execution lanes (FDM CPU, FDM GPU, FEM CPU, FEM GPU), and materialized Zarr/binary outputs.
svg.text: Fullmag Architecture: Authored Intent to Four-Lane Execution
Explicit separation of scene identity, physics modules, ProblemIR requested intent, planner legality gate, and resolved lane provenance
Target intent only; never triggers implicit physics
Identity only: name/type never activate physics
Material(Ms, A, α, Ku, Kc, D) · MaterialParameterField
LLG time evolution (heun, rk4, rk23, rk45, abm3)
Variational law: δEk = −μ0 ∫ Ms Hk · η dV
Summed into Heff = ∑ Hk inside LLG RHS
Single Gilbert → explicit conversion: (TG + α m×TG)/(1+α2)
Explicit PhysicsGraph dependency edges in IR
Cell link Aab vs surface energy σsurf = −J1(ma·mb) − ...
Single canonical IR shared by Python & Control Room
• Strict GPU guard: never silent CPU fallback
Rejects malformed SI, conflicts, unsupported lanes
Aborts before execution; zero silent degradation
• Concrete integrator, demag operator, PBC pairs
Cartesian SoA grid · open FFT & multilayer
MFEM shared mesh (Ωm ⊂ Ωa) · P1 / prism
m, Heff, Hk, u, Jc on native FDM grid or FEM mesh
